blocks.en: TCP by itself is insecure against network attackers. Someone on the network (e.g. a malicious router, an attacker sniffing packets on a wire) could read or even modify your TCP packets while they’re in transit.
blocks.zh_html: 单独使用 TCP 时，它无法抵御网络攻击者(network attackers)。网络中的某个人，例如恶意路由器(malicious router)，或在线路上嗅探分组(sniffing packets)的攻击者，可能在 TCP 分组(TCP packets)传输途中读取甚至修改它们。

blocks.en: Also, with TCP, you might connect to an attacker instead of the real server. Suppose you want to connect to a bank website, and you do a DNS lookup for www.bank.com. The attacker (e.g. someone who hacked into the resolver or a router) changes the DNS response so that it maps www.bank.com to the attacker’s IP address, 6.6.6.6. Now, when you form a TCP connection to the bank website, you’re talking to the attacker. You might end up sending your bank password to the attacker!
blocks.zh_html: 此外，使用 TCP 时，你可能连接到攻击者，而不是真正的服务器(server)。假设你想访问一家银行网站，并对 www.bank.com 进行 DNS 查询(DNS lookup)。攻击者，例如入侵了解析器(resolver)或路由器(router)的人，篡改 DNS 响应(DNS response)，让 www.bank.com 映射到攻击者的 IP 地址 6.6.6.6。现在，当你与银行网站建立 TCP 连接(TCP connection)时，实际上是在和攻击者通信。你最终可能把银行密码发给攻击者。

blocks.en: To address these security issues, we add a new protocol, Transport Layer Security (TLS), on top of TCP.
blocks.zh_html: 为了解决这些安全问题，我们在 TCP 之上加入一种新协议：传输层安全协议(Transport Layer Security, TLS)。

blocks.en: TLS can be thought of as a Layer 4.5 protocol, sitting in between TCP and application protocols like HTTP. (We use a weird number like 4.5 because the obsolete Layers 5 and 6 have nothing to do with security.) TLS relies on the bytestream abstraction of TCP, so it doesn’t think about individual packets or packet loss/reordering. TLS provides the exact same bytestream abstraction to applications as TCP does, but the bytestream is now secure against network attackers. This is why HTTP and HTTPS are semantically identical protocols. The only difference is that HTTPS runs over the secure bytestream of TLS-over-TCP, while HTTP runs over raw TCP with no TLS.
blocks.zh_html: 可以把 TLS 看作第 4.5 层协议(Layer 4.5 protocol)，位于 TCP 和 HTTP 这类应用协议(application protocols)之间。我们使用 4.5 这样有点奇怪的编号，是因为已经过时的第 5 层和第 6 层与安全性无关。TLS 依赖 TCP 的字节流抽象(bytestream abstraction)，因此它不关心单个分组(packet)，也不直接处理丢包(packet loss)或重排序(reordering)。TLS 向应用提供与 TCP 完全相同的字节流抽象，但这个字节流现在能够抵御网络攻击者(network attackers)。这就是为什么 HTTP 和 HTTPS 在语义上是相同协议；区别只在于 HTTPS 运行在 TLS-over-TCP 的安全字节流(secure bytestream)之上，而 HTTP 直接运行在没有 TLS 的原始 TCP(raw TCP)之上。

blocks.en: To distinguish between HTTPS and HTTP, we use Port 80 for HTTP connections, and Port 443 for HTTPS connections. Servers can force users to use HTTPS by replying to all Port 80 requests with a redirect to use Port 443 instead.
blocks.zh_html: 为了区分 HTTPS 和 HTTP，我们使用端口 80(Port 80)承载 HTTP 连接，使用端口 443(Port 443)承载 HTTPS 连接。服务器(server)可以通过把所有端口 80 请求都重定向(redirect)到端口 443，强制用户使用 HTTPS。

blocks.en: At a high level, TLS uses cryptography to encrypt messages sent over the bytestream. TLS also uses other cryptographic protocols (message authentication codes) to prevent attackers from changing messages as they’re sent over the network.
blocks.zh_html: 从高层看，TLS 使用密码学(cryptography)对通过字节流(bytestream)发送的消息进行加密(encrypt)。TLS 还使用其他密码学协议(cryptographic protocols)，例如消息认证码(message authentication codes)，防止攻击者在消息通过网络传输时篡改它们。

blocks.en: In order to encrypt traffic, TLS must start with an additional handshake to exchange keys and verify the identity of the server (e.g. real bank, not someone impersonating the bank).
blocks.zh_html: 为了加密流量(traffic)，TLS 必须先执行一个额外的握手(handshake)，用于交换密钥(keys)并验证服务器身份(identity)，例如确认对方是真正的银行，而不是冒充银行的人。

blocks.en: Because TLS is built on top of TCP, the TCP three-way handshake first proceeds as normal. This creates an (insecure) bytestream, allowing all future messages, including the TLS handshake, to proceed without thinking about individual packets.
blocks.zh_html: 由于 TLS 构建在 TCP 之上，TCP 三次握手(three-way handshake)会先按正常流程进行。这会创建一个不安全的字节流(bytestream)，使后续所有消息，包括 TLS 握手(TLS handshake)，都可以在不考虑单个分组(packet)的情况下继续进行。

blocks.en: The TLS handshake can now proceed:
blocks.zh_html: 接下来，TLS 握手(TLS handshake)可以开始：

blocks.en: The client and server exchange hellos. The hellos contain random numbers, which ensures that every handshake results in different secret keys. (It would be bad if we used the same key every time, and attackers hacked us and learned that key.) The hellos also allow the client and server to agree on specific cryptographic protocols to use. The client’s hello lists all cryptographic schemes the client supports, and the server’s hello picks one to use.
blocks.zh_html: 客户端(client)和服务器(server)交换 hello 消息。hello 中包含随机数(random numbers)，确保每次握手都会产生不同的秘密密钥(secret keys)。如果每次都使用同一个密钥，而攻击者入侵后学到了这个密钥，那会很糟。hello 还允许客户端和服务器协商要使用的具体密码学协议(cryptographic protocols)。客户端的 hello 会列出客户端支持的所有密码学方案(cryptographic schemes)，服务器的 hello 则从中选择一个。

blocks.en: The server sends a certificate of authenticity. This will allow the client to verify that it’s talking to the real server, and not an impersonator. There’s a bit of complexity in how the client actually verifies this certificate, which we won’t discuss here.
blocks.zh_html: 服务器(server)发送一个真实性证书(certificate of authenticity)。这使客户端(client)能够验证自己正在与真正的服务器通信，而不是与冒充者(impersonator)通信。客户端实际如何验证这个证书(certificate)有一些复杂细节，这里不展开讨论。

blocks.en: The client and server derive a secret that only the two of them know. Since the bytestream is still insecure at this point, they’ll need a cryptographic protocol that enables sharing a secret over an insecure channel. We won’t discuss the details here, but if you’re familiar with RSA public-key encryption (e.g. from CS 70 at UC Berkeley), that’s one possible cryptographic scheme to use here. The client encrypts a secret with the server’s public key and sends it to the server. Only the server knows the corresponding private key and is able to decrypt the message and learn the secret.
blocks.zh_html: 客户端(client)和服务器(server)推导出一个只有双方知道的秘密(secret)。由于此时字节流(bytestream)仍然不安全，它们需要一种密码学协议(cryptographic protocol)，能够在不安全信道(insecure channel)上共享秘密。这里不讨论细节；如果你熟悉 RSA 公钥加密(public-key encryption)，例如在 UC Berkeley 的 CS 70 中学过，那么它就是这里可用的一种密码学方案(cryptographic scheme)。客户端用服务器的公钥(public key)加密一个秘密并发送给服务器。只有服务器知道对应的私钥(private key)，因此只有服务器能够解密消息并获得这个秘密。

blocks.en: The client and server derive secret keys based on the shared secret and the random values from the hellos. Using the secret ensures that attackers can’t learn the secret keys. Using the random values ensures that we derive a different key every time. This derivation is done locally and independently by both the client and server. The secret keys are never actually sent across the network, so the attacker has no chance to learn them.
blocks.zh_html: 客户端(client)和服务器(server)基于共享秘密(shared secret)以及 hello 中的随机值(random values)推导秘密密钥(secret keys)。使用这个秘密可以确保攻击者无法学到秘密密钥；使用随机值则确保每次都会推导出不同的密钥(key)。这个推导过程由客户端和服务器在本地独立完成。秘密密钥实际上从不会通过网络发送，因此攻击者没有机会学到它们。

blocks.en: The client and server exchange some acknowledgements to confirm that they derived the same secrets, and nobody tampered with the messages sent over the network so far (since the bytestream is still insecure).
blocks.zh_html: 客户端(client)和服务器(server)交换一些确认(acknowledgements)，以确认双方推导出了相同的秘密(secrets)，并确认到目前为止通过网络发送的消息没有被篡改(tampered with)，因为此时字节流(bytestream)仍然是不安全的。

blocks.en: At this point, the handshake is complete, and all future messages are encrypted with the secret key (message authentication codes are also used to prevent tampering). We have now established a secure bytestream on top of the TCP connection, and applications can exchange data on top of our secure bytestream.
blocks.zh_html: 到此为止，握手(handshake)完成，之后所有消息都会用秘密密钥(secret key)加密，同时也会使用消息认证码(message authentication codes)防止篡改。我们已经在 TCP 连接(TCP connection)之上建立了一个安全字节流(secure bytestream)，应用(applications)可以在这个安全字节流之上交换数据。
